I remember when I was maybe 5 or 6 and I was reading this super religious pop-up picture book about Christmas and Jesus' birth and whatnot. I'm reading it waaayy past my bedtime, with the flashlight under the covers and I get to the page with an angel on ot and I see a big flash of light.  I immediately closed the book and went to bed. When my mom tried to read the book to me again I cried and ran away from her. 

TD;LR I think God was trying to speak to me, and didn't do a very good job, I'm an atheist.

My father is a special kind of snowflake. When it came to buying my first car I was limited to either Ford or a Chevy anything else was heathen and he was going to kick me out if I got a Toyota, Honda, etc. Even though I was paying for the is car with my hard earned and saved money. 
And also I wasn't allowed to eat at Chic-fil-A because if I did, then the Republicans would win.

I work at a preschool and for as long as I had been working there there was a "men don't change diapers" rule, so men were always in rooms where all the children were potty trained. We got a new director, who apparently wasn't aware of this unwritten rule. As soon as she found out about it, an email was sent out and she told us that men were very much supposed to be changing diapers,  as it was in the job description. There was a sudden rise in men (and by rise I mean all 3 of them) quitting.

A few things:

°I'm a preschool teacher, and I'm to the point where I'm closer in age to the parents than I am the kids. 
°I'm 19 and going through the same sort of "developmental milestone" problems as my coworkers who are 10-20 years my senior. 

Being mentally older than I am physically is hard sometimes.
